summary: The Muse week 1 delivery writer passes the security review at 19359dd1 with seven nonblocking findings. Approval entries cannot steer paths: a zod schema refuses any file name that is not a plain name, and row ids are matched against the picture list before use and never form a path. All checks run before the first write, a different existing manifest and a different existing delivery file are refused for both color and line, SHA-256 values come from the delivered bytes, the writer invents no review, and the path holds no credential read, shell, or network. The findings are provenance, path containment, and write-boundary hardening items on operator-controlled inputs.
nonblocking_findings: RB8-01 Major data integrity: the deliver CLI pins no picture-list SHA-256, unlike render and verify which pin PICTURE_LIST_V3_SHA256; the manifest provenance rests on an unpinned list file. Rationale: Green recorded the gap as an open point (plan.md:1437 and 1467). (code reading; confirmed)

RB8-02 Major path containment: --delivery and --muse accept absolute or parent-relative paths, so a run can write outside out/ and outside the repository; the stricter reading of spec.md:54-55 and contract.md:353 forbids this; the writer performs no containment check and Green's own smoke used /tmp. (code reading; confirmed)

RB8-03 Nit write boundary: writes use existsSync plus writeFile, not exclusive creates; a dangling symlink at a delivery target would receive the delivered PNG bytes outside deliveryRoot; phase-2 RB-03 mandated flag wx for the smoke writer. (code reading; probe blocked by tool permission)

RB8-04 Nit duplicate picture-list names within one run can silently overwrite an earlier copy; both copies pass the pre-write existence check before any write, so the manifest then records a SHA-256 that no delivered file matches. (code reading; probe blocked by tool permission)

RB8-05 Nit degenerate list line-art names: dot and manifest.json pass the plain-name basename check; dot can break the refusal-leaves-the-folder-unchanged claim on a first run (partial copy, no manifest), and manifest.json as a line name would be clobbered by the final manifest write. (code reading; probe blocked by tool permission)

RB8-06 Nit Muse reads follow symlinks out of museRoot; there is no realpath or regular-file check, unlike the --raw rule at contract.md:346-347; impact is bounded by the PNG size and format checks. (code reading; probe blocked by tool permission)

RB8-07 Nit test gap: T152 to T161 cover no path or validation refusal (traversal name, symlink, duplicate list name, malformed list); a mutation dropping the MuseFileName refine would keep the suite green. (code reading; confirmed)

Scope: phase_base_sha 15a7bf0b2a59b8137a05805666df6736dc256167 (plan.md:1418 and 1429). Green commits f41fe108 (code) and 7b843204 (evidence) with Green role base 0bf8858a. Tests: bash heavy-run.sh -c 'node_modules/.bin/vitest run tests/storytime-muse-delivery.test.ts --maxWorkers=1' exited 0 with Test Files 1 passed (1) and Tests 10 passed (10), Duration 10.82s. No exit 75.

Path handling (code reading; confirmed): MuseFileName refuses any approval file name whose basename differs from the name, and refuses dot and dot-dot. Approval row ids must equal a picture-list row id or the run stops; the writer never forms a path from a row id. Delivery copy targets come only from row.fileName and row.lineArtFileName, and fileName is pinned by the pattern ^l2-w\d{2}-[a-z-]+-v\d+\.png$ in the list loader and planPictureRow; the writer also requires the line-art name to be a plain name.

Overwrite and deletion (code reading; confirmed): the writer deletes nothing. A different existing manifest.json is refused; an existing delivery file with different bytes is refused; the refusal loop covers both the color and the line copies. A second run with the same inputs writes the same bytes (T161).

Input validation (code reading; confirmed): MuseApprovalListSchema parses the list before use; a malformed list, a missing version, or a missing checkedBy stops the run with the failing path in the message. Unknown entry fields are stripped by zod defaults, not injected.

Secrets (code reading; confirmed): muse-delivery.ts imports only node:crypto, node:fs, node:fs/promises, node:path, sharp, zod, and book-pictures.js. It reads local files only, with no fetch, no child process, no env read, and no credential. The deliver CLI errors pass the redactSecrets 500-character boundary in scripts/storytime-book-pictures.ts. The Muse key lives only in scripts/storytime-muse.mjs at run time and is not reached from this path.

Evidence integrity (code reading; confirmed): colorSha256 and lineSha256 are computed from the same byte buffers the writer copies, and the manifest records them on the candidate and lineArt entries. mapReviews refuses a non-pass verdict, maps only a Kimi review and a named person review, and the person schema requires a non-empty checkedBy with evidenceClass owner-passed or person-checked, so a model class cannot stand in for a person.

A2: not triggered. The delivery hands fictional-character pictures to Workbooks; no named real person or school is published and no bucket upload or public release exists. A residual note, not a finding: a row with zero review artifacts is delivered with status ready and reviews empty, which Red T153 and T159 codify; a stricter gate needs a PM contract change because decision 2 sends contract changes through the PM.
A6: measure/tracks.md at 19359dd1 lists this track as [~] with no security-resolved claim, so the registry does not overstate the state.

Probe status: the sandbox denied probe scripts (writes under /tmp, heredocs, and tsx -e programs containing dynamic import were refused by tool permission). RB8-03, RB8-04, and RB8-05 rest on code reading only; RB8-01, RB8-02, RB8-06, and RB8-07 were confirmed by code or test reading. The working probe pattern for a later session is a short static-import tsx -e program that imports /home/daniebo/Desktop/advantage-forge/src/storytime/muse-delivery.ts.
The task adds no endpoint, authentication boundary, tenant scope, migration, or secret store.
